title: Hiring Big Chief Moore, the trombonist who took his shoes off
summary: Morgan says he was the first to hire Big Chief Moore, an Indian trombonist, and recalls him taking his shoes off to play.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You say he was here on a show? He wrestled Big Chief Moore?
Yeah, a little bit. I doubt if he knows me. He was here and you gave him a job or something, huh?

Yeah, I was the first man to hire him. Hire him from the Lyrics Theater. He was taking him up to Vashville. That's the first job he played. He was taking off his shoes, man, to play. That guy played some trombone though that night.
Did Moore come from Oklahoma or someplace up there? Do you know? Who? This Indian trombone player.
I don't know where he's from.
He's a FEMA Indian. He's from New Mexico or Arizona.
No, he's from New Mexico or Arizona, not too far. Yeah.
Boy where he could play. Mm-hmm.
What did he do with his shoes off? Did he play the trombone with his feet or something?
No, he'd take the shoes off, rest his feet.
Oh. I thought maybe he was one of those trick trombones. You've seen those guys.
No, he wanted to take his shoes off. And he said, you're going to hear some trombone playing now, boy. Take my shoes off. And he pulled them shoes off and rest them dogs. I mean he played too.
